guitar.notes: J Mascis is strongly associated with the Fender Jazzmaster (including his own signature model), a well-documented guitar/guitarist pairing.

tone.target: lo-fi fuzzed indie punk crunch with ragged power chords
tone.profile: lo-fi fuzzed indie punk crunch with ragged power chords
tone.summary: A gritty, high-gain signal chain utilizing Fuzz for the core tone, followed by a British amp model (UK 45) to provide classic punk crunch, finished with a robust cabinet and slight room ambience.
corrections: use raw Dinosaur Jr. fuzz crunch
keep it gritty, not Tube Screamer

rig.name: Dinosaur Jr. - Freak Scene - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up stray noise inherent in high-gain fuzz tones.
blocks.gap: None. Gate 2 is suitable for general noise gating.

blocks.purpose: Provide the core raw, aggressive fuzz and sustain required for Dinosaur Jr.'s signature sound.
blocks.gap: None. Fuzz is essential for this genre/artist.

blocks.purpose: Slightly boost the signal into the amp to maintain power and punch without adding clarity (acting as a clean booster).
blocks.gap: The Boost module is used here primarily for level matching, not tone shaping.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the classic British punk/garage rock sound (Marshall style) needed for raw crunch and punch.
blocks.gap: None. UK 45 is ideal for this genre's aggressive, mid-focused tone.

blocks.purpose: Provide the necessary physical cabinet resonance and punch associated with punk/garage rock.
blocks.gap: None. This cab choice complements the UK 45 amp model well.

blocks.purpose: Sculpt the tone by boosting upper mids to achieve 'bright upper mids' and controlling excessive low-end mud.
blocks.gap: None. EQ is necessary for tonal shaping in high-gain contexts.

blocks.purpose: Add a subtle sense of space and 'lo-fi' grit without sounding polished or modern.
blocks.gap: Room reverb is used sparingly to add atmosphere, avoiding the overly clean sound associated with plate/spring.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism by swapping the current IR for a more open, loose-sounding 4x12 that better captures lo-fi punk grit.

proposals.recommendedAsset: loose/open 4x12 IR (e.g., vintage tweed or open mic)
proposals.reason: The current cab is too tight; a looser IR will enhance the lo-fi, ragged punk sound.
proposals.expectedGain: More natural room resonance and less boxy tone.
